messages:
nina: alert — ap-east1 showing intermittent GPU attach failures and very high nvme trim latency since 04:07 UTC. small jobs okay, batch attach retries up.

omar: looking at the node traces now. saw lots of async TRIM calls queuing behind metadata writes. controllers report `async trim timeout` for some namespaces.

henry: paste from dmesg on one repro node: ```nvme0n1: async trim timed out: cmd=0x00 status=0x9 lba=0x7f2a```

storage-bot: Detected anomaly: 22 nodes with trim latency > 10s, 40 drives with program-erase cycles nearing threshold. Pool: ap-east1-ephemeral-c.

omar: hypothesis — last night's disk firmware GC parameters + our aggressive background TRIM overlap with janitor scrubs/backfills. Results: excessive device GC leading to long write stalls.

henry: mitigation idea: 1) disable background async TRIM on ephemeral volumes for 2 hours, 2) throttle janitor scrubs and backfills, 3) temporarily mark region constrained for >8GPU launches.

ops-qa: routing rule ready. I'll block job placements with gpus>8 into ap-east1 for 120m. Small launches unaffected.

nina: implemented temporary sysctl on hosts to disable async discard: `echo 0 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/discard_granularity` (rolling) — testing on 5 nodes first.

janitor-bot: janitor config change proposed by henry applied: `scrub_rate_limit_mb_s=10`, `max_parallel_scrubs=1`.

storage-bot: post-change metrics (10m after): trim-time 99th dropped 78% on canaries, gpu_attach_failures down from 96->6 in probe window.

vendor-support: noted similar behaviour with FW 6.1.2 when async discard concurrent with background GC. Recommends FW 6.2.0 which staggers GC windows. Planning maintenance window required.

henry: cost/ops note — if we keep region constrained we'll need to shift ~60 queued GPUs to us-west for 3 hours. Estimated incremental spend ~$2.4k/hr. Suggest we use spare reserved pool first.

omar: next steps: 1) keep async discard disabled for 2h while we schedule firmware canary, 2) stagger janitor/backfill windows, 3) vendor to run firmware canary on 3 hosts in 45m.

nina: opening incident doc and tagging product on potential SLA impacts. Will update when vendor confirms canary slot. :white_check_mark:
